event: Reactor power reduction initiated for scheduled safety test
Power reduction halted; grid operator requests continued electricity supply
operational_notes: Emergency Core Cooling System (ECCS) isolated at this point
physics_notes: ECCS isolation a safety violation; not relevant to accident causation but indicative of culture

event: Grid operator releases reactor; power reduction resumes
physics_notes: 11-hour delay at 1600 MWt while ECCS remained isolated

event: Power reduction finally resumed after shift handover
physics_notes: Night shift takes over with test still pending
Gradual reduction toward test target of 700-1000 MWt

event: Unexpected power collapse during transfer to local automatic control
operational_notes: Operator possibly reset the setpoint incorrectly; Xe-135 poisoning plays role
physics_notes: Xenon-135 (t1/2=9.2h) had accumulated during high-power operation; strong neutron absorber suppressed power; positive void coefficient irrelevant at this power

event: Power stabilized at 200 MWt; operators decide to proceed with test at reduced power
operational_notes: Operating reactivity margin (ORM) = 8 rods inserted equivalent; minimum required = 15
physics_notes: 8 rods ORM violates operating procedures; insufficient negative reactivity reserve; test should have been aborted

event: Additional main coolant circulation pump (MCP) activated
physics_notes: Pump 12 started; increased coolant flow reduces steam void fraction temporarily

operational_notes: 8 of 8 MCPs now running; coolant flow at maximum
physics_notes: High flow reduces steam voids; reduces positive void feedback temporarily; but also reduces margin to boiling

event: ORM formally checked and recorded at 8 rods
operational_notes: Shift foreman signs off on proceeding
physics_notes: 8 rods = ~700 MW(t) worth of negative reactivity; minimum for safe operation is 15 rods; this is documented safety violation #2

event: Test begins; steam turbine generator feed valves closed
physics_notes: Reduced coolant flow as turbine winds down; steam void fraction rises; positive void coefficient begins amplifying reactivity; power starts to increase

event: Emergency SCRAM (AZ-5) button pressed by operator Leonid Toptunov
operational_notes: All control rods commanded to insert
physics_notes: Graphite displacer tips on control rods insert first; 1-2 second positive reactivity pulse before neutron-absorbing sections reach core; this is the design defect

event: Power excursion rate emergency protection signals triggered
operational_notes: Reactor protection system registering uncontrolled power rise
physics_notes: Positive void coefficient and graphite tip effect create compounding positive reactivity; control rods slow and jam before reaching bottom

event: Fuel element rupture; steam explosion; second explosion (possibly partial nuclear excursion)
operational_notes: 1000-tonne reactor lid (Elena plate) ejected; core exposed to atmosphere
physics_notes: Peak power estimated at ~30000 MWt = 10x design; prompt criticality exceeded; fuel fragmented; steam explosion from contact of fragmented fuel with water; second explosion possibly steam or hydrogen or limited nuclear excursion — disputed

event: Graphite fire begins; radioactive plume initiated
physics_notes: Plume direction shifted with wind over 10 days; total release extended April 26 - May 5; I-131 release peaked Day 1 (704 PBq) then declined
Population received dose during delay; average thyroid doses elevated

event: Graphite fire extinguished after sand/boron/lead aerial drops
physics_notes: Total I-131 release by May 5: ~1760 PBq; Cs-137: ~85 PBq
